title: adaptive-model-fallback-and-fanout-proxy-integration-playbook-2026
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This playbook describes recommended integration patterns, configuration examples, and operational runbook items for customers that want to deploy an adaptive model-fallback strategy using a fanout/proxy layer in front of Redwood Inference endpoints. The goal is to provide resilient, cost-aware routing that maintains SLOs while exposing deterministic controls to platform engineers.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: Customer success engineers, platform engineers, SREs integrating Redwood inference into production services.
- Applies to: Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments where a proxy/fanout layer is used for model routing, A/B, or capacity-tier fallbacks.
- Not covered: Internal kernel/runtime tuning; see eng-serving-runtime docs for low-level optimizations.

Motivation and outcomes:
- Reduce user-visible errors during model upgrades, regional outages, or capacity limits.
- Automatically route or fanout requests to secondary model variants when primary routes exceed latency or error thresholds.
- Provide cost control by routing non-critical workloads to cheaper quantized variants.
- Emit consistent telemetry for billing, evaluation, and QBRs.

Key concepts:
- Primary/Secondary model variants: Named endpoint or model version pairs configured with compatibility metadata (token limits, format expectations).
- Fanout proxy: The intermediary service that can replicate requests (read-only checks, shadowing) or route requests to a single back end.
- Adaptive policy engine: Evaluates runtime signals (latency p50/p95, error rate, token spend) and decides to failover, degrade quality, or throttle.
- Deterministic fallback: A predictable and auditable mapping (e.g., primary->fallback-quantized->fallback-llm2) so rollbacks and billing attribution are safe.

Pre-integration checklist (customer-side):
1) Identify primary request classes and SLOs (latency p95, availability target, max per-request cost).
2) Ensure model compatibility: prompt schemas, function-calling contracts, and tokenization behaviors.
3) Provision Redwood API keys and endpoint mapping for the primary and fallback model endpoints; record model versions.
4) Define telemetry tags that will be used by the proxy to annotate requests (tenant_id, route_id, fallback_reason, model_variant).
5) Agree on billing attribution policy with finance (how fallback calls are charged when triggered by the platform).

Architecture patterns (3 recommended):
A) Thin router with deterministic failover (low complexity)
- Behavior: Proxy routes single request to primary; upon configurable error/timeout/failure policy, sequentially retries to fallback variants.
- Use when: Small latency overhead budget, deterministic cost expectations.
- Pros: Predictable billing, simple tracing.
- Cons: Potential delay on failover path.

B) Concurrent fanout with race policy (parallel first-success wins)
- Behavior: Proxy issues parallel requests to primary and one or more fallback variants; first successful response is returned.
- Use when: Ultra-low tail-latency is critical and extra cost is acceptable for cold starts.
- Pros: Best p99 latency in many failure modes.
- Cons: Higher token cost and complexity in deduplication.

C) Shadowing + sampling for quality regression detection
- Behavior: Primary responses are returned to users; the same request is sent asynchronously (shadowed) to fallback/experimental variants for offline evaluation.
- Use when: Deploying new quantized models or tuned prompt sets; requires acceptance testing.
- Pros: Safe production testing; collects eval signals.
- Cons: Requires storage for shadow traces and eval pipeline.

Configuration examples
- Example router decision YAML (thin router):

router:
  default_policy: sequential_failover
  timeout_ms: 1200
  retries: 0
  model_priority:
    - name: redwood-prod/gptx-1.0
      max_tokens: 2048
      tag: primary
    - name: redwood-prod/gptx-quant-1.0
      max_tokens: 2048
      tag: fallback-quant
    - name: redwood-open/llm-lite-0.9
      max_tokens: 1024
      tag: fallback-lowcost
  signals:
    latency_p95_threshold_ms: 900
    error_rate_threshold_pct: 2.0
  telemetry_tags:
    - tenant_id
    - route_id
    - fallback_reason

- Example concurrent fanout JSON snippet (proxy):

{
  "strategy": "concurrent_fanout",
  "fanout_targets": [
    {"model": "redwood-prod/gptx-1.0", "weight": 0.7},
    {"model": "redwood-prod/gptx-quant-1.0", "weight": 0.3}
  ],
  "response_policy": "first_success",
  "dedupe_id_header": "X-Request-Id",
  "cost_cap_usd": "5.00"
}

Telemetry and SLOs to monitor (suggested):
- Per-route p50/p95/p99 latency (primary and fallback metrics separated).
- End-to-end error rate (4xx vs 5xx split) and fallback-trigger rate.
- Token spend per tenant per day and per-request token delta when fallback occurs.
- Shadow-eval regression rate: percentage of shadow requests that fail automated quality checks.
- Fanout duplicate suppression failures and occurrence of partial responses.

Suggested alert thresholds:
- Primary route p95 > 1.5x SLO for 5m -> P1 alert to SRE + CS on-call
- Fallback-trigger rate > 5% of total requests for 15m -> P2, investigate capacity or model degradation
- Token spend rate > expected burn rate by 20% -> Finance notification and temporary throttling

Operational runbook (triage steps)
1) If p95 spikes on primary route:
  a) Confirm if latency is localized (single region/tenant) or global via per-region dashboards.
  b) Check Redwood runtime health (model queue lengths, GPU load) and fanout proxy logs for timeout reasons.
  c) If primary is degraded and the proxy policy is sequential_failover, validate fallback responses are compatible with request schema.
  d) If immediate mitigation needed, update router to route to fallback-quant for affected routes and annotate in the incident.
2) If error rate increases and appears across variants:
  a) Pull recent prompts for top failing requests (use sampled traces).
  b) Validate prompt format/metadata changes from client code.
  c) Engage model-onboarding team if regression ties to model update.
3) If concurrency/deduplication failures observed in fanout:
  a) Inspect dedupe_id header propagation (X-Request-Id) and retry logic in client.
  b) Enable temporary sampling at 10% with shadowing disabled to reduce duplicate workload.

Compatibility and contract checklist
- Function/tool calling: ensure the fallback model supports invoked function schema or proxy will need to transform calls.
- Tokenization: annotate expected token usage per model in the router config.
- Response format: fallback variants must preserve critical structured fields or proxy must map/normalize them.
- Idempotency: client should set idempotency keys for non-idempotent side effects; proxy must forward key to all fanout targets if parallel.

Security and privacy considerations
- PII in shadowing: do not enable shadowing for requests flagged as sensitive unless destination model is permitted (see security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention).
- API keys: store Redwood credentials in a secrets manager; rotate keys per customer policy. Proxy should use short-lived tokens for upstream calls.
- Audit logging: annotate fallback_reason in audit logs and include model_variant to support billing and compliance requests.

Cost control knobs
- Cap fanout concurrency per tenant and enforce a per-tenant daily token cap.
- Use cheaper quantized models for sampled traffic and non-interactive routes (batch scoring).
- Configure the router with a cost_cap_usd to prevent runaway spend during incidents.

Testing and rollout plan
1) Local integration smoke tests: unit tests for header propagation, idempotency, and timeout handling.
2) Canary rollout: route 1% traffic through the proxy policy with shadowing enabled for secondary models. Verify metrics for 48 hours.
3) Incremental ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 20% over monitored windows, verifying shadow-eval pass rate and token spend.
4) Full switch with feature-flag toggle and ability to rollback in under 5 minutes.

Example test checklist (pass/fail criteria):
- 1000 synthetic requests: 0 critical schema mismatches returned by fallback.
- Shadow-eval difference in key metric (e.g., hallucination rate) < 3% over baseline.
- p99 end-to-end latency increase < 15% when concurrent fanout is enabled at 5% sampling.

Troubleshooting matrix (top issues):
- Symptom: Fallback returns truncated function-call JSON.
  Cause: Fallback model max_tokens lower than primary.
  Action: Increase max_tokens on fallback config or add post-processing normalization.

- Symptom: Unexpected cost spike during outage.
  Cause: Concurrent fanout without cost_cap or retries multiplied by proxies.
  Action: Disable parallel fanout; revert to sequential_failover and contact customer success.

- Symptom: Shadow-eval storage backlog.
  Cause: No downstream consumer or storage throttling.
  Action: Pause shadowing; provision temporary storage and backfill once consumer is restored.

Ownership and contacts:
- CS integration lead: Aisha Patel (author) — for playbook questions and live cutovers.
- Runtime escalation: eng-serving-runtime on-call (see runbooks).
- Model compatibility: Model Onboarding team (model-onboarding).
- Security review/approvals: security-and-compliance team.

Appendix A — Example proxy health check CLI
# curl health check to proxy
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $PROXY_TOKEN" https://proxy.example.com/health | jq

Appendix B — Minimal sample router change for emergency rollback (CLI snippet)
# set route to fallback-quant immediately
redwood-routerctl set-route --route-id orders-completion --policy sequential_failover --model redwood-prod/gptx-quant-1.0 --annotation "emergency-rollback"
